expectations.text: By the end of the run, docs/intent/previews/previews-design.md makes 2Q the eviction policy. A run whose first turn stops at an earlier phase's review (for example an HLD stop) before reaching this design also passes if its reply names 2Q as the choice the design will carry.
expectations.evidence: Private Cache section now describes 2Q concretely

expectations.text: Where the previews design is updated, its Decisions & Alternatives table gains a row for the eviction policy that names 2Q, at least one rejected alternative (LRU or aged frequency), and the accepted cost (extra queues / bookkeeping, or the queue-size split to tune).
expectations.evidence: The team accepted 2Q's extra queue bookkeeping and size-split tuning as the cost of protecting comparison sheets

expectations.text: The first reply does not offer, suggest, or ask about writing a decision doc for the eviction policy, despite the long debate the user describes.
expectations.evidence: Want a full decision doc instead (`docs/intent/previews/decisions/eviction-policy.md`), or is the table row enough?

expectations.text: The first turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes1.patch`) and writes no standalone decision-doc content into another file.
expectations.evidence: no file under decisions/ in changes1.patch; only design/HLD files touched

expectations.text: Asked whether the choice deserves a decision doc after the long debate, the reply recommends the Decisions row as enough, and grounds that in the choice affecting only the previews node (nothing else is built around it), not in the debate having been settled. Offering to write one anyway if the user still wants it is fine.
expectations.evidence: I agree it earns one — that decision stays genuinely live for a cold reader

expectations.text: The follow-up turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes.patch` against `changes1.patch`): the user asked for an opinion, not for a doc.
